narrative_markdown:
## Today's Forecast

Warm temperatures dominate the day with a high of 30°C (86°F) expected. Thunder possible from the morning, peaking this evening. Early Mostly cloudy gives way to Partly cloudy at midday and returns to Mostly cloudy by evening. Winds shift from a northeasterly overnight to a southwest by midday, reaching gusts of 36 km/h (19 kt) ashore. The UV index will peak at 9.3. Air quality is moderate with an AQI of 67 from the Kisumu Airport station. As of 06:01, reports through 04:00: no rain; no thunder; high so far 21°C (70°F); low so far 20°C (68°F); peak sustained 11 km/h (6 kt); sky mostly cloudy.

## Extended Outlook

Temperatures and winds much the same through Saturday, with showers and thunderstorms possible Thursday, and rain and thunderstorms likely from Friday. Skies partly cloudy Thursday, then mostly cloudy Friday and Saturday. Saturday's call: rain, 100%, with all four models wet; highs around 30°C (85°F). Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) calls it dry. At this lead Best Match has the best record, right 87% of the time over 81 checks.

Further out, temperatures and winds much the same through Wednesday, with showers and thunderstorms likely Sunday, Monday and Tuesday, and showers and thunderstorms possible Wednesday. Sunday and Monday: all four models wet, highs around 30°C (86°F). Tuesday: all three models that reach it wet, highs around 28°C (82°F).

Only GFS, ECMWF and ICON reach past Monday. ICON is the wetter solution from Sunday to Monday; GFS, ECMWF and UKMO keep it drier. Wednesday's call: rain, 100%, with both models wet; highs around 28°C (83°F). At this lead ECMWF has the best record, right 83% of the time over 77 checks.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential

Peak CAPE values indicate thunderstorm potential, with Best Match (1650 J/kg), ECMWF (1500 J/kg) and UKMO (2100 J/kg) above the thunderstorm threshold, peaking at 20:00. Any thunderstorm could produce sudden gusts well above the forecast 36 km/h (19 kt), posing a brief wind hazard.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters

Overnight winds are east-northeasterly at 8 km/h (4 kt) gusting to 12 km/h (6 kt), turning southwesterly by midday at 7 km/h (4 kt) gusting to 16 km/h (9 kt), and increasing to 10 km/h (5 kt) gusting 17 km/h (9 kt) into the evening, with a peak gust of 29 km/h (16 kt). Thunderstorm gusts could exceed these values when thunderstorms develop.

## Detailed Discussion

### Synoptic Overview

Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the north (1007 hPa) and highest toward the southeast (1014 hPa) — a 7 hPa spread, a moderate large-scale gradient. Pressure is also falling toward the south-southwest, a large-scale feature building in that direction, though speed cannot be stated. Pressure overhead is falling. BASIN PRESSURE: today’s mean sea-level pressure sits between 1012.1 and 1014.5 hPa, falling by 1.7 hPa over three days. The CALL notes a pressure trend of -1.6 hPa, with the lowest pressure toward the north.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes

The REVIEW finds no model meaningfully better at Day+0, though GFS misses the thunderstorms and over-forecasts clouds and highs, while Best Match under-forecasts daytime highs and peak wind. The CALL’s high of 30°C (86°F) aligns with the model range of 29–32°C (84–90°F), but Best Match sits on the wrong side of its own rain record, being slightly under-forecast. KMD predicts a max of 29°C (84°F) and light showers, slightly cooler than the CALL’s 30°C (86°F) high and isolated evening showers, showing modest disagreement. DATA SUFFICIENCY notes 62 checks for Day+0, providing a settled picture despite uneven model coverage, supporting confidence in the overall guidance.
